NASA Space Apps 2026 · Harmonization of MODIS and VIIRS hot spots

Two decades of fire from orbit, recorded on two scales that don't agree.

Satellites have tracked active fire hotspots since 2000, but the record is split between MODIS and VIIRS, whose detections can't be compared directly. Emberline converts both to daily burning presence on one grid, calibrates VIIRS to MODIS, and turns the result into a burning-activity calendar for any area, so responders, scientists and land managers can see when burning usually peaks and when a season is running outside its norms.

The problem

The same fires, counted three different ways

Fire managers need to know when a region normally burns and whether this season is unusual. A 25-year satellite record could answer that, but every sensor change rewrites the scale. These three panels use real NASA FIRMS detections over Australia from .

01 · Sensitivity

VIIRS sees far more fire pixels than MODIS

02 · Drift

MODIS itself is no longer the instrument it was

03 · Consequence

Stitching the records invents burning

Evidence

Does it work? Scored on real data and on known truth

Real-data checks hold out data the model never saw. The simulated record adds what real data can't give: the exact answer a stable MODIS would have recorded every year.

Real · predicting MODIS from VIIRS, Australia FIRMS NRT

Each week is held out, the model refit on the others, and that week's MODIS burning area predicted from VIIRS alone.

Real · finding industrial heat sources FIRMS SP

The persistence filter runs blind on 8 months of VIIRS over southern India, then is scored against FIRMS's own static-source labels[7].

Real · how far ahead the outlook helps MODIS 2005–19

Every past year replayed week by week against a climatology built without it. Skill is the error reduction versus assuming a typical year, inside each state's fire season.

Real · calibration uncertainty bootstrap

The VIIRS→MODIS calibration refit 40 times on resampled weeks. The band on every harmonised line comes from this spread.

Simulated · 25-year record vs truth known answer

Simulated · held-out years and fire-type split known answer

Method

From hotspots to a calendar

Each step is a module in the open-source pipeline; the browser re-runs the calendar maths for whatever area you draw.

1 · Daily presence, not counts

Detections from both sensors are binned to a 0.25° cell and a local solar day (UTC shifted by longitude/15 h). The unit is the cell-day: burning or not. Pixel counts never cross the sensor boundary.

2 · Remove non-vegetation heat

FIRMS type flags drop volcanoes, static sources and offshore platforms[2]. A persistence mask then learns ~1 km bins that burn on too many days, which catches flares and smelters in NRT data that carries no flag.

3 · Calibrate VIIRS to MODIS

Over the overlap a logistic model predicts whether MODIS flags a cell-day from S-NPP features: pixel count, fire radiative power, night share, and activity on adjacent days and cells. Strata are region × land cover[8], shrunk toward their parents when thin.

4 · Keep the record stable

Only S-NPP is the VIIRS reference, so NOAA-20 and NOAA-21 launches don't raise the series; NOAA-20 fills S-NPP outages. Terra-only 2000–02 is scaled to Terra + Aqua. As Terra and Aqua drift and retire[10], the calibrated VIIRS line carries the MODIS scale forward.

5 · Calendar and anomalies

Season and critical windows are the shortest circular runs of weeks holding 80 % and 50 % of mean activity, so Southern-Hemisphere seasons that cross New Year work. Anomalies use leave-one-out medians and MAD with a noise floor.

7 · Outlook and uncertainty

The 1–4 week outlook carries the last four weeks' anomaly forward, damped by how much past years' anomalies actually persisted. Its skill is measured by replaying every past year against a climatology built without it. Calibration uncertainty comes from refitting on resampled weeks or years (block bootstrap).

6 · Agricultural vs wildfire

Detections form space-time events. Cropland share, calendar recurrence (same cell, same weeks, other years), size, duration and FRP give each event a probability of being an agricultural burn.

Build it yourself

Open pipeline, Python 3.11+

Every number on this page is produced by these commands. A scheduled workflow re-pulls the key-less FIRMS feeds every six hours and republishes the page.

make setup        # pip install -e '.[api,dev]'
make data         # FIRMS mirror, MODIS history, Natural Earth, NASA textures
make australia    # real 5-satellite harmonisation + weekly cross-validation
make static-check # filter vs FIRMS static-source labels
make demo         # 25-year simulated record vs known truth
make web test     # this page, then the test suite
make serve        # FastAPI: POST /calendar, GET /live?bbox=…
